turns.answer_text:
I used the POSCAR structures to compare crystal symmetry, local coordination, bond-direction anisotropy, and composition—not formula alone. This matters because the training data include polymorphs with substantially different birefringence. Cubic candidates were assigned approximately zero birefringence.

My selected candidates are:

| Rank | Candidate | Formula | Predicted Δn at 1064 nm | Distance from 0.1 |
|---:|---|---|---:|---:|
| 1 | **c012** | Li₂ZnGa₂Se₅ | ≈0.099 | ≈0.001 |
| 2 | **c013** | Li₂ZnGa₂Se₅ | ≈0.099 | ≈0.001 |
| 3 | **c096** | Li₂MgGa₂Se₅ | ≈0.103 | ≈0.003 |
| 4 | **c071** | AlCuGeSe₄ | ≈0.104 | ≈0.004 |
| 5 | **c020** | TaCu₃Se₃S | ≈0.095 | ≈0.005 |

The first three are supported by the related Li–Mg/Zn–Ga–Se training structures, with their distinct bonding geometries used to distinguish polymorphs. For **c071**, the structure matches the GaCuGeSe₄ prototype: transferring the Ga→Al change observed in the structure-matched Ag–Sn selenides gives approximately  
\(0.12323+(0.04624-0.06585)=0.10362\).  
For **c020**, the ordered S/Se environment breaks cubic optical isotropy and supports a moderate predicted birefringence near the target.

These are model estimates; validation errors are on the order of a few hundredths, so the fine ordering is uncertain.

Final: c012, c013, c096, c071, c020
